knowledgePattern: Reduce complementary trigonometric inputs before quadratic range optimisation

hints.title: Compare the whole inputs
hints.body: Check whether the sine and cosine arguments are complementary. This can reduce the expression to one trigonometric function.
hints.recap: Work with the entire trigonometric input, and use the exact attained range of sine or cosine after simplifying.
hints.pitfall: The input includes its coefficient and phase shift.
hints.pause: Simplify g and find its attained range.

recall.reminder: Work with the entire trigonometric input, and use the exact attained range of sine or cosine after simplifying.

hints.title: Optimise on that range
hints.body: Regard the outer expression as a quadratic in the value of g. Complete the square and compare its permitted vertex with both endpoints.
hints.recap: The inner range restricts which points of an outer quadratic are attainable.
hints.pitfall: The largest and smallest inputs need not give the largest and smallest outputs.
hints.pause: Find both extreme output values and then their product.

recall.reminder: The inner range restricts which points of an outer quadratic are attainable.

solution:
1. The two trigonometric arguments add to π/2, so cos(π/3−3x/2)=sin(π/6+3x/2). Thus g(x)=32(1+sin(3x/2+π/6)).

2. Sine attains every value in [−1,1], so g attains every value in [0,3]. Put t=g(x).

3. The target is 4t−t2−3=1−(t−2)2. On 0≤t≤3, its maximum is 1 at t=2 and its minimum is −3 at t=0; the other endpoint gives 0.

4. The product is 1·(−3)=−3. Answer A.
